analysis.title: US Equity Positioning Update
key_insights: Systematic investors sharply cut equity exposure last week after the volatility spike following the US midterm elections.
Risk Control funds cut equity risk to their lowest level in a year, down from the 69th percentile the prior week.
CTAs accelerated selling and moved net short equities for the first time since March, with exposure in the 5th percentile.
Risk Control, CTAs and leveraged ETF selling combined to produce $365 bn of excess sell flow, the largest on record.
Hedge funds chased the rally on Wednesday, adding to Momentum and Quality factors and buying Hyperscalers.
After Thursday's price action, hedge fund sells outpaced buys almost 6:1 and gross exposure fell to the 25th percentile for the past year.
Tech took the brunt of hedge fund de-risking: net exposure in key AI complex sectors fell to year-to-date lows, and Tech net exposure fell to the 8th percentile for the past year.
Friday showed signs of risk being added back, and Monday's index-level recovery may mark the start of some re-risking.

UBS describes the setup as cleaner: de-risking has removed near-term supply while potential demand builds from underweight composite managers, buyback restarts, improved retail flows and net foreign buying.
Corporates are expected to buy roughly $50 bn of stock next week as they emerge from buyback blackouts.
UBS says near-term risk/reward for US equities is increasingly skewed to the upside with positioning reset and volatility declining.
Overall hedge fund long/short ratio is back near the lows, and composite manager positioning is underweight, a potential source of demand.
Key year-end risk events listed are CPI, NVDA earnings, NFP and FOMC.

sector_views.rationale: Hedge fund net exposure to Tech fell to the 8th percentile for the past year and AI complex exposure hit year-to-date lows, which UBS frames as removed supply rather than a directional call.

earnings_insights: NVDA earnings is listed among key year-end risk events. No estimates or figures are given.
risk_factors: Year-end risk events: CPI, NVDA earnings, NFP and FOMC.
Re-risking is early. UBS cites only Friday and Monday as signs of risk being added back.
vol_and_positioning: Risk Control funds' equity exposure is at its lowest level in a year, down from the 69th percentile a week earlier.
CTA equity exposure is net short for the first time since March, in the 5th percentile.
Risk Control, CTAs and leveraged ETFs produced $365 bn of excess sell flow, the largest on record.
Hedge fund gross exposure fell to the 25th percentile for the past year, with sells outpacing buys almost 6:1 on Thursday.
Hedge fund Tech net exposure is in the 8th percentile for the past year, and AI Winner exposure is back at the summer lows.
Hedge fund long/short ratio is back near the lows.
Composite managers remain underweight, which UBS flags as a possible source of demand.
Volatility is declining after the post-midterm spike.
geopolitical: US midterm elections triggered a volatility spike and systematic de-risking.

tension_points.bull_case: De-risking removed near-term supply while demand builds from underweight composite managers, about $50 bn of buybacks, improved retail flows and net foreign buying, so risk/reward skews to the upside.
tension_points.bear_case: Hedge fund sells outpaced buys almost 6:1 on Thursday, AI complex exposure is at year-to-date lows and re-risking is only tentative after Friday and Monday.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A renewed volatility spike or a negative surprise from the listed year-end events (CPI, NVDA earnings, NFP, FOMC) would undercut the re-risking case.
